# Wardley map syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-wardley/grammar/wardley.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Wardley map syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `wardley-beta` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed Wardley maps with Langium (`wardley.langium` and
`common.langium` in `@mermaid-js/parser`); the rules below are its token rules, in its order,
and its grammar.

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text; and a line break appended. Keywords are case-sensitive.

The first rule that matches wins, and no keyword gives way to a longer name: `notebook` is
`note` and the name `book`, `buyer` is `buy` and `er`, so no unquoted name can start with a
keyword or a strategy (D423); quote such names. A name is words of letters, digits, `_`, `&`,
`(`, `)` and `-`, separated by blanks: `Cup of Tea` is one name. Each statement ends its line,
except that `wardley-beta` may share its line with the first one.

Coordinates are `[visibility, evolution]`, each a decimal with a `.`: up to 1 a fraction of
the axis (`0.5` is half way, `1.0` is the end), above 1 a percentage (`1.5` is 1.5 %, D428),
above 100 an error.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A map is `wardley-beta`, then statements, each on a line of its own (the first may share
the header's line). The `YAML`, `DIRECTIVE` and `COMMENT` tokens of the lexer are skipped
before parsing.

```ebnf
wardley = { NEWLINE } Header { NEWLINE | statement NEWLINE } [ statement ] EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = WARDLEY_BETA ;
```

```ebnf
statement = Size
          | Evolution
          | Anchor
          | Component
          | Link
          | Evolve
          | Pipeline
          | Note
          | Annotations
          | Annotation
          | Accelerator
          | Deaccelerator
          | Title
          | AccTitle
          | AccDescr ;
```

```ebnf
name = STRING
     | ID
     | NAME ;
```

`[visibility, evolution]`, both decimals.

```ebnf
coordinates = LBRACKET DECIMAL COMMA DECIMAL RBRACKET ;
```

```ebnf
coordinate = DECIMAL
           | INT ;
```

```ebnf
labelOffset = LABEL LBRACKET [ DASH ] INT COMMA [ DASH ] INT RBRACKET ;
```

`size [width, height]`, whole pixels.

```ebnf
Size @Size = SIZE LBRACKET INT COMMA INT RBRACKET ;
```

`evolution A -> B -> …`: the stage names, each with an optional `@boundary` and `/ name`.

```ebnf
Evolution @Evolution = EVOLUTION stage ARROW stage { ARROW stage } ;
```

```ebnf
stage = name [ AT DECIMAL ] [ SLASH name ] ;
```

```ebnf
Anchor @Anchor = ANCHOR name coordinates ;
```

`component Name [visibility, evolution]`, then `label [x, y]`, a strategy and `inertia`,
in that order, each optional.

```ebnf
Component @Component = COMPONENT name coordinates [ labelOffset ] [ LPAREN STRATEGY RPAREN ] [ INERTIA | LPAREN INERTIA RPAREN ] ;
```

`A -> B`: a link, with optional flows after either name and a `; label`. Without an arrow
the names must be quoted (`"A" "B"`), since unquoted words run into one name.

```ebnf
Link @Link = name [ LINK_PORT ] [ LINK_ARROW | ARROW ] name [ LINK_PORT ] [ LINK_LABEL ] ;
```

```ebnf
Evolve @Evolve = EVOLVE name DECIMAL ;
```

`pipeline Parent {`, then at least one component per line, then `}` on its own line.

```ebnf
Pipeline @Pipeline = PIPELINE name LBRACE NEWLINE { NEWLINE } PipelineComponent NEWLINE { NEWLINE } { PipelineComponent NEWLINE { NEWLINE } } RBRACE ;
```

```ebnf
PipelineComponent @PipelineComponent = COMPONENT name LBRACKET DECIMAL RBRACKET [ labelOffset ] ;
```

```ebnf
Note @Note = NOTE STRING coordinates ;
```

```ebnf
Annotations @Annotations = ANNOTATIONS LBRACKET coordinate COMMA coordinate RBRACKET ;
```

```ebnf
Annotation @Annotation = ANNOTATION INT COMMA LBRACKET coordinate COMMA coordinate RBRACKET STRING ;
```

```ebnf
Accelerator @Accelerator = ACCELERATOR name coordinates ;
```

```ebnf
Deaccelerator @Deaccelerator = DEACCELERATOR name coordinates ;
```

`title Tea Shop`: the title drawn at the top (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | LBRACKET | `\[` |  |  |
| INITIAL | COMMA | `,` |  |  |
| INITIAL | RBRACKET | `\]` |  |  |
| INITIAL | AT | `@` |  |  |
| INITIAL | SLASH | `\/` |  |  |
| INITIAL | LPAREN | `\(` |  |  |
| INITIAL | RPAREN | `\)` |  |  |
| INITIAL | DASH | `-(?!>\|->\|\.->\|--[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?---(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S)))` |  | `-` before a label offset: `label [-10, 5]`. A `->`, `-->`, `-.->` or `---` block starting here is that token instead (mermaid@12's longer alternatives of `-`). |
| INITIAL | LBRACE | `\{` |  |  |
| INITIAL | RBRACE | `\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | DECIMAL | `[0-9]+\.[0-9]+` |  | A coordinate or boundary: a decimal such as `0.5`, with digits on both sides of its `.`; up to 1 a fraction of the axis, above 1 a percentage. |
| INITIAL | ARROW | `->` |  | `->`: a link from one component to another, or the next evolution stage. |
| INITIAL | LINK_PORT | `\+<>\|\+>\|\+<` |  | `+>`, `+<` or `+<>`: a flow along a link (forward, backward or both ways), after either name. |
| INITIAL | LINK_ARROW | `-->\|-\.->\|>\|\+'[^']*'<>\|\+'[^']*'<\|\+'[^']*'>` |  | A link's arrow: `-->`, `-.->` (dashed) or `>`, or a labelled flow such as `+'label'>`, `+'label'<` or `+'label'<>`. |
| INITIAL | LINK_LABEL | `;[^\n\r]+` |  | `; label`: a link's label, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | STRATEGY | `build\|buy\|outsource\|market` |  | `(build)`, `(buy)`, `(outsource)` or `(market)` after a component: how it is sourced. |
| INITIAL | WARDLEY_BETA | `wardley-beta` |  | `wardley-beta`: starts a Wardley map. |
| INITIAL | SIZE | `size` |  | `size [1100, 800]`: the map's width and height in pixels (the last one wins). |
| INITIAL | EVOLUTION | `evolution` |  | `evolution Genesis -> Custom -> Product -> Commodity`: the stages along the evolution axis, at least two; `Name@0.3` sets where a stage ends, `Name / Second` gives it two names. |
| INITIAL | ANCHOR | `anchor` |  | `anchor User [0.95, 0.5]`: a user or need the map starts from, at `[visibility, evolution]`. |
| INITIAL | COMPONENT | `component` |  | `component Tea [0.8, 0.6]`: a component at `[visibility, evolution]`, then optionally `label [x, y]`, a strategy such as `(build)`, and `inertia`. Inside a pipeline it has only its evolution: `component Gas [0.3]`. |
| INITIAL | LABEL | `label` |  | `label [x, y]`: moves a component's label by `x`, `y` pixels. |
| INITIAL | INERTIA | `inertia` |  | `inertia` or `(inertia)` after a component: it resists change. |
| INITIAL | EVOLVE | `evolve` |  | `evolve Kettle 0.8`: the evolution a component is moving to (the last one per component wins). |
| INITIAL | PIPELINE | `pipeline` |  | `pipeline Kettle { … }`: the components of a pipeline, one per line, each `component Name [evolution]` on the parent's visibility. |
| INITIAL | NOTE | `note` |  | `note "text" [0.3, 0.5]`: a note on the map. |
| INITIAL | ANNOTATIONS | `annotations` |  | `annotations [0.1, 0.9]`: where the box that lists the annotations goes (the first one wins). |
| INITIAL | ANNOTATION | `annotation` |  | `annotation 1, [0.5, 0.5] "text"`: a numbered marker on the map, listed in the box. |
| INITIAL | ACCELERATOR | `accelerator` |  | `accelerator Cloud [0.5, 0.8]`: a force that speeds evolution up. |
| INITIAL | DEACCELERATOR | `deaccelerator` |  | `deaccelerator Legacy [0.5, 0.3]`: a force that slows evolution down. |
| INITIAL | NAME | `(?!title\s\|accTitle\|accDescr)[A-Za-z](?:[A-Za-z0-9_()&]\|-(?!>))*(?:[\t ]+[A-Z…` |  | A name: words of ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `&`, `(`, `)` and `-` (not before `>`), separated by blanks; never starting with `title` and a blank, `accTitle` or `accDescr`. |
| INITIAL | — | `[\t ]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accDescr: …` (the rest of the line) or `accDescr { … }` (over lines, to `}`): the accessible description of the map. mermaid@12's one rule, as two tried in order; the block's `[\s\S]*?\}` is its `[^}]*\}`, written so that line-based highlighters read the block as one span. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr\s*\{[\s\S]*?\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `[\t ]*accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the map, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `[\t ]*title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …`: the title drawn at the top of the map, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | INT | `0\|[1-9][0-9]*(?!\.)` |  | A whole number such as `10`: a size, a label offset, an annotation's number, or an annotation coordinate (`1` is 100 %); no leading zeros. |
| INITIAL | STRING | `"(?:[^"\\]\|\\.)*"\|'(?:[^'\\]\|\\.)*'` |  | A quoted name or text: `"…"` or `'…'`; `\` escapes the next character, and it may span lines. |
| INITIAL | ID | `\w(?:[-\w]*\w)?` |  | A name of ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-` that no other rule reads (one that starts with `_`, or `accTitleX`). |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE | `\r?\n` |  |  |
| INITIAL | YAML | `---[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?---(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `---` … `---` block inside the body: skipped. |
| INITIAL | DIRECTIVE | `[\t ]*%%\{[\S\s]*?\}%%(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `%%{…}%%` left in the text the lexer reads: skipped. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `[\t ]*%%[^\n\r]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line, after other text: a comment. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
